recentItems.description: Nina Carberry rode an Irish Grand National winner and some top horses in a distinguished 17-year career in the saddle and its fantastic to see the MEP back on the track and successful in the Pat Smullen Cancer Trials Ireland Charity Race on a special afternoon at the Curragh.

recentItems.title: BetMGM Solario Stakes: Alfred Wallace joins rich roll of honour | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Alfred Wallace put his experience to good use when running out a narrow winner of the BetMGM Solario Stakes at Sandown.

Ed Walker’s two-year-old was making his seventh appearance of the season in a Group Three contest that had a notable late absentee in hot favourite Rock Montreal, who was taken out on account of the deteriorating conditions.

Alfred Wallace had impressed when winning the Listed Pat Eddery Stakes at Ascot last month and having since finished fourth in Acomb Stakes at York, he was an 11-4 shot to get back on the winning trail at Group Three level just 10 days later.

Kieran Shoemark kept things simple on the chestnut son of Dubawi, positioning him on the heels of the pacesetting Sonic Angel before taking over and committing for home two furlongs from the finish.

While some of his less experienced rivals took a while to find their stride and wandered when coming under pressure, Alfred Wallace stayed straight and true and had enough up his sleeve to see off Dover Street by half a length, with Breacher the same distance further behind in third.

Walker said: “What a dude, he’s an absolute star to back up 10 days after York.

“I was really cross when I saw the entries for this as the plan was always to come straight here, but I got tempted by York and probably didn’t give Aidan’s horse (Haffner) the respect he deserved.

“When I saw the entries for this I had to put him in and spent my week kicking myself for going to York, but what a tough little horse – he helped me out of trouble.”

The Lambourn handler plans to give Alfred Wallace a shot at Group One glory before the season is out, adding: “You can’t see a rib on him, he’s been busy and never leaves an oat. He’s always fresh as paint at home and he’s got such a great appetite for it.

“A few high-profile non-runners probably helped us there but I see William Muir every morning and he thinks the world of his horse who was third (Breacher).

“Our fellow just has that battle-hardened experience, he’s small and strong and tough. I’ve not trained many Dubawis and people always mention their constitution and that is what this fellow has.

“He’s got his Listed and Group Three wins now and that is massively important to owners Rockcliffe Stud.

“I think by the law of physics he will find life tougher next year when the more backward horses are coming out and that is why we are squeezing the lemon a little bit this year.

“We’ll definitely have a shot at a Group One with him, he’s in everything and I’ll just have to try not to run him in all of them!”

recentItems.title: Nina Carberry rolls back the years with emotional charity win | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Like old times!

MEP Nina Carberry enjoyed a 17-year career as a rider and rode the likes of Gold Cup winner Don Cossack in his formative years as well as winning races such as the Irish Grand National.

Teaming up with old ally Gordon Elliott, Carberry partnered Ndaawi to success in the Pat Smullen Cancer Trials Ireland Charity Race at the Curragh in a feelgood story supporting Ireland's biggest charity raceday which has raised over €1.2m for a wonderful cause in honour of the multiple champion jockey who we sadly lost back in September 2020 at the age of 43.

recentItems.title: Zavateri set for Champions Day after Celebration Mile romp | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Eve Johnson Houghton was thrilled to see her stable star Zavateri stamp his class on the Virgin Bet Celebration Mile at Goodwood.

A Group One-winning juvenile in last season’s National Stakes, the Without Parole colt had endured a frustrating three-year-old campaign so far, with an early-season setback ruling him out of a potential Classic bid.

He performed creditably to finish fifth in both Goodwood’s Sussex Stakes last month and the City of York Stakes on the Knavesmire just last week, and he was the 11-10 favourite to strike Group Two gold seven days later.

After being settled in midfield by Charlie Bishop, Zavateri quickened up smartly in the rain-softened ground to claim the lead with a furlong still to run and the further he went the better he looked, eventually passing the post with three-and-a-half lengths in hand over Qirat.

“On hearing the ground was heavy I said to Charlie ‘are we going to run’ and he said, ‘let’s see’. I said if he goes on the ground he would win and he did,” said Johnson Houghton.

“He is from very small beginnings but has developed into a machine, and he showed the turn of foot I knew he had.”

Zavateri is set for an immediate jump to the highest level, with the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on Champions Day at Ascot (October 17) uppermost in his trainer’s mind.

She added: “Now he will go the the QEII, end of conversation. We need to go back to Group One company at Ascot I’m really keen to do that.

“We (father Fulke Johnson Houghton) won it twice with Rose Bowl a long time ago (1975 and 1976) and it’s the right race for this horse.”

recentItems.title: Sea Of Rain "my Oaks filly," says Jim Bolger | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Jim Bolger is planning a trip to Doncaster’s St Leger meeting with Sea Of Rain following her victory in the Newtownanner Stud Irish EBF Stakes at the Curragh.

The Naval Crown filly was the most experienced in the 10-strong field with six previous runs under her belt, only one of which she had won.

She was an 18-1 shot stepping up to Group Three level under Colin Keane, but raised her game to score by three-quarters of a length from Ballyskeagh.

Bolger said: “I’m kicking myself – I intended backing her when I saw the 25-1 but I forgot about it. I’m the worst punter in the world!

“It’s no surprise. All she needed was the mile and a gallop. I’ve been telling the lads she’s my Oaks filly for next year.

“That’s only Colin’s second ride for me. I’d say we’ll go for the May Hill at Doncaster. I won it years ago with Turret Rocks (2015).”

In his interview with Racing TV, the legendary trainer could not hide his enthusiasm for his filly and for her prospects over middle distances next year as another Classic contender looks to have been unearthed from Coolcullen.

recentItems.title: Guineas horse? Push The Boat Out remains unbeaten at the Curragh | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Push The Boat Out got up in the dying strides to claim the notable scalp of Royal Ascot hero Great Barrier Reef in the Heider Family Stables Round Tower Stakes at the Curragh.

Making his first appearance since completing a hat-trick in the Coventry Stakes in June, 4-5 favourite Great Barrier Reef was sent straight to the front by Ryan Moore, with Livenka disputing the lead during the early stages the Group Three contest.

The market leader set sail for home two furlongs out and had the field strung out as the Michael O’Callaghan-trained Push The Boat Out – a course and distance winner on his debut three weeks ago – gave chase entering the final furlong.

Seamie Heffernan timed his challenge on the 17-2 shot to perfection, wearing Great Barrier Reef to hand him his first defeat by a neck.

O’Callaghan said: “When they win a maiden first time out they have to jump up to this level. There was a little bit of greenness there during the middle part of the race and he came off the bridle early, but Seamie got him rolling from halfway.

“Seamie was very complimentary of him – he said he was a racehorse. We’ll get him home and see how he is but he said he’s still a little bit weak.

“Obviously he’s unbeaten, he’s won his Group race and he’s beaten the Coventry winner. Seamie mentioned Newmarket so we’ll get him home and let the dust settle.

“We’ll enjoy today.”

recentItems.title: Group 1 aim for Love Dynasty after 33/1 Atalanta triumph | Full Race | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Kevin Ryan is planning a step up to the highest level with Love Dynasty following her surprise success in the BetMGM Atalanta Stakes at Sandown.

Winner of her first two starts for William Haggas, the daughter of Dubawi moved north last year and while she has performed admirably in Listed and Group-race company, she had failed to add to her tally.

Making her first appearance since chasing home Sparks Fly in the Princess Elizabeth Stakes at Epsom in early June, Love Dynasty was a widely unconsidered 33-1 shot for this Group Three test under Neil Callan.

The previously unbeaten Secret Of Life took the field along for much of the one-mile journey and looked to have most of her rivals in trouble halfway up the straight, but she was eventually reeled in, with Love Dynasty doing best of the closers to score by a neck from Noche Clasica.

While the result was a shock for many, Ryan insists he was hopeful of a bold showing after the rain arrived in Esher.

“It wasn’t a shock to me. The most important thing for her is the ground – she needs soft ground, that’s why she’s so lightly-raced,” said Hambleton-based trainer.

“She’s a very consistent filly who leaves everything out on the track. It’s great for Steve Parkin of Clipper (Logistics, owner), he has a nice broodmare band, all he wants to do is add quality to them and she will hopefully.

“In fairness to William (Haggas), when she came to me, he said he always thought a lot of her. She just has to have some soft in the ground and when she gets that she’s a top-class filly.”

Love Dynasty will now be aimed at the Sun Chariot at Newmarket on October 3 if conditions are suitable.

Ryan added: “I’ve made an entry at Newmarket for her in the Group One and if I didn’t think a lot of her, I wouldn’t have done that.

“As long as the ground is suitable, she’ll probably go there next.”

Callan said: ” I thought coming here a stiff mile, I’m going to hoof her out and then hold a position and then when she hits her flat spot I’ll be able to kick her through it without losing any ground through it. It all went perfectly well, really smooth.

“I went the economical route up the inside and I just wanted a nice clean passage to keep the momentum rolling. Once I got her through her flat spot between the two furlong pole and the one I gave her a couple of flicks and I knew from the furlong pole she will gallop out powerfully to the line.

“It’s an association that goes back a long way, Kevin is my old boss and Steve Parkin of Clipper Logistics is a great friend and supporter of mine.

“I’m a bit of a part-time jockey and I probably get more of a kick out of my sons. They are flying along Jack and Henry, so ‘team Callan’ is doing great and hopefully the day I do turn up and ride still I can make my mark like I’ve done today.”

recentItems.title: Sandown & Goodwood Preview | Saturday Best Bets & Tips | The Racing TV Podcast
recentItems.description:
Dan Barber and Martin Dixon look back at York and through Saturday's cards at Sandown, Goodwood, Beverley and the Curragh.

Roger Varian joins to talk about Rock Montreal ahead of the Solario, the progressive Barstow at Sandown, and a season with a strike rate he's delighted with. Eve Johnson Houghton explains the quick turnaround for Zavattari in the Celebration Mile, with the QE2 potentially next. 

Andrew Cooper, clerk of the course at Sandown, on watering through a difficult summer, the badgers, and where the ground stands going into the weekend. Jane Mangan previews the Curragh, including an eighteen-runner Irish Cambridgeshire.

recentItems.title: Gihan Arnolda: From Homeless at 12 to Training in Newmarket | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Josh Stacey meets Gihan Arnolda in Newmarket, twenty-five years after he arrived in the town having never sat on a horse.

Born in East London to Sri Lankan and Portuguese parents, Gihan lost his mother young and was homeless on and off between the ages of twelve and fourteen, sleeping in shop doorways. Taken into care and later fostered, he watched racing on television with his foster father and applied to the racing school on the strength of it — having fallen off a pony on Wimbledon Common the day before he went.

Nine weeks later he was named most improved. Six months after that he rode a winner at Thirsk. This summer he sent out his first winner as a trainer, Damascus Steel at Goodwood.

He talks about the trainers who shaped him — Chris Wall, Roger Varian and Peter Chapple-Hyam — the yard he now runs with his partner Charlotte, what racing looked like to a young man from multicultural London arriving in Newmarket in the late 1990s, and what he'd say to anyone watching who thinks it isn't possible.

recentItems.title: The Verdict: Ebor Festival Review | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Angus McNae and Josh Kerr go through the Sky Bet Ebor Festival at York, looking past the results at the times, the pace and the tactics that shaped them.

On day one, Item won the Juddmonte International in a race where the early pace shaped everything, and the ride on Constitution River comes in for scrutiny.

Day two brought slower times as the ground went against the runners, with Sun Goddess the standout — impeded in running and still finishing through the line strongly in Harry's Half Million.
